questions.q:
With reference to the Regulating Act of 1773, consider the following statements:
1. It made the Governor of Bengal the Governor-General of Bengal.
2. It established a Supreme Court at Calcutta.
3. It allowed servants of the Company to carry on private trade.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Act designated the Governor of Bengal as Governor-General and set up the Supreme Court at Calcutta (1774). It prohibited Company servants from private trade and from accepting gifts or bribes, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.q: The principle of open competition for recruitment to the Indian Civil Service was introduced by which one of the following?
questions.e: The Charter Act of 1853 ended the Company's patronage and threw the civil service open to competition (Macaulay Committee, 1854). The 1833 Act had stated the principle on paper but it was never put into practice.

questions.q:
Which of the following were introduced by the Government of India Act, 1919?
1. Dyarchy in the provinces
2. A bicameral legislature at the Centre
3. Provincial autonomy
4. An All-India Federation
questions.e: The 1919 Act (Montagu-Chelmsford) brought dyarchy in provinces (transferred and reserved subjects) and a bicameral central legislature (Council of State and Legislative Assembly). Provincial autonomy and the federation scheme came with the 1935 Act.

questions.q: Which one of the following was NOT a feature of the Government of India Act, 1935?
questions.e: The 1935 Act extended the vote to only about 10 per cent of the population. It did give provincial autonomy, dyarchy at the Centre, bicameralism in six of eleven provinces and a Federal Court.

questions.q:
With reference to the Constituent Assembly of India, consider the following statements:
1. It was constituted under the scheme formulated by the Cabinet Mission Plan, 1946.
2. Dr Sachchidananda Sinha was elected its permanent President.
3. Members from the provinces were elected by the provincial legislative assemblies, with seats allotted roughly in proportion to population.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Sachchidananda Sinha was only the temporary (interim) President at the first meeting on 9 December 1946. Dr Rajendra Prasad was elected permanent President on 11 December 1946. Statements 1 and 3 are correct (about one seat per million, indirect election).

questions.q:
Which of the following committees of the Constituent Assembly were chaired by Jawaharlal Nehru?
1. Union Powers Committee
2. Union Constitution Committee
3. Provincial Constitution Committee
4. Rules of Procedure Committee
questions.e: Nehru chaired the Union Powers and Union Constitution Committees. Sardar Patel chaired the Provincial Constitution Committee, and Rajendra Prasad chaired the Rules of Procedure Committee.

questions.q:
Which of the following provisions of the Constitution came into force on 26 November 1949 itself?
1. Provisions relating to citizenship (Article 5)
2. Fundamental Rights (Part III)
3. Provisions relating to the provisional Parliament (Article 379)
4. Election Commission (Article 324)
questions.e: Articles 5-9 (citizenship), 60, 324, 366, 367, 379-391, 392 and 393 took effect on 26 November 1949. The rest of the Constitution, including Part III, commenced on 26 January 1950.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Preamble:
1. In the Berubari Union case (1960), the Supreme Court held that the Preamble is a part of the Constitution.
2. In the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973), the Supreme Court held that the Preamble is a part of the Constitution.
3. The Preamble has been amended only once so far.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Berubari held the Preamble is not a part of the Constitution. Kesavananda reversed that view. The only amendment is the 42nd Amendment (1976).

questions.q:
Which of the following words were added to the Preamble by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976?
1. Socialist
2. Secular
3. Democratic
4. Integrity
questions.e: The 42nd Amendment added 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity'. 'Democratic' was in the original text.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT mentioned in the Preamble to the Constitution of India?
o: Equality of status and of opportunity
Fraternity assuring the dignity of the individual
Liberty of belief, faith and worship
questions.e: 'Equality before the law' is in Article 14. The Preamble speaks of 'equality of status and of opportunity'.

questions.q:
Which of the following are unitary (non-federal) features of the Indian Constitution?
1. Single citizenship
2. Integrated judiciary
3. Rigid amendment procedure for all provisions
4. Appointment of State Governors by the President
questions.e: Single citizenship, an integrated judiciary and Governors appointed by the Centre are unitary features. The amendment procedure is a mix: some provisions need only a simple majority, so it is not rigid for all provisions.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs of features of the Indian Constitution and their sources:
1. Concurrent List: Australia
2. Residuary powers with the Centre: Canada
3. Fundamental Duties: Ireland
4. Emergency provisions: Weimar Constitution of Germany

How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Fundamental Duties came from the Constitution of the USSR. Ireland is the source of the DPSP, the method of Rajya Sabha nominations and the Presidential election method.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the Golaknath case (1967), the Supreme Court held that Parliament cannot amend Fundamental Rights.
2. The Kesavananda Bharati case (1973) overruled the Golaknath ruling.
3. In Minerva Mills (1980), the Court held that the limited nature of Parliament's amending power is itself part of the basic structure.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: All three are correct. Kesavananda allowed amendment of any provision, including Fundamental Rights, but not so as to destroy the basic structure. Minerva Mills struck down clauses of the 42nd Amendment on this basis.

questions.q:
With reference to Articles 2-4 of the Constitution, consider the following statements:
1. Parliament can form a new State by a simple majority.
2. A law made under Article 3 is treated as an amendment of the Constitution under Article 368.
3. A Bill under Article 3 needs the President's recommendation, and he must refer it to the affected State legislature for its views.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Article 4 says laws under Articles 2 and 3 are not amendments under Article 368, so a simple majority is enough. The State legislature's views are sought but are not binding on Parliament.

questions.q: Transfer of a part of Indian territory to a foreign country requires:
o: a law of Parliament under Article 3, passed by simple majority
an executive order of the President under Article 73
a law under Article 2 with the consent of the State concerned
questions.e: In re Berubari Union (1960), the Supreme Court held that Article 3 covers only internal readjustment among States. Ceding territory to another country needs an amendment under Article 368. The 9th Amendment (1960) followed.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The States Reorganisation Commission (1953) was headed by Fazl Ali.
2. The Dar Commission (1948) recommended the reorganisation of States on a linguistic basis.
3. The JVP Committee (1948) did not favour the formation of States on a linguistic basis at that time.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Dar Commission advised reorganisation on administrative convenience, not language. The JVP Committee (Nehru, Patel, Pattabhi Sitaramayya) also held back. Andhra (1953) was the first linguistic State, after Potti Sriramulu's fast, which led to the SRC.

questions.q: The Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956 abolished the classification of States into Parts A, B, C and D. As a result of the reorganisation, India had:
questions.e: After the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 and the 7th Amendment, there were 14 States and 6 Union Territories.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding citizenship under the Constitution:
1. Provisions on citizenship are contained in Part II.
2. Article 11 empowers Parliament to regulate the acquisition and termination of citizenship.
3. The Constitution exhaustively provides for acquisition of citizenship after 1950, leaving no role for Parliament.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Articles 5-9 deal with citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution. Article 11 leaves later regulation to Parliament, which enacted the Citizenship Act, 1955.

questions.q:
With reference to the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019, consider the following statements:
1. It applies to Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, Parsis and Christians from Afghanistan, Bangladesh and Pakistan.
2. It covers such persons who entered India on or before 31 December 2014.
3. It reduces the residence requirement for their naturalisation from eleven years to five years.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: All three are correct. Such persons are not treated as illegal migrants, and the Act exempts certain areas (Sixth Schedule tribal areas and Inner Line Permit areas).

questions.q:
Under the Citizenship Act, 1955, citizenship can be lost through which of the following?
1. Renunciation
2. Termination
3. Deprivation
4. Continuous stay outside India for five years
questions.e: The Act provides three modes of losing citizenship: renunciation (voluntary), termination (on voluntarily acquiring another country's citizenship) and deprivation (compulsory, by the Central Government). Long absence is not a ground.

questions.q:
Which of the following rights are NOT available to an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) cardholder?
1. Right to vote
2. Eligibility for government employment
3. Lifelong multiple-entry visa to India
4. Right to hold constitutional offices such as President
questions.e: An OCI is not a citizen. The OCI cannot vote, hold constitutional posts or take government employment. The lifelong multiple-entry visa is one of the benefits an OCI does get. OCI is not dual citizenship.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Doctrine of Eclipse:
1. It applies to pre-Constitution laws that are inconsistent with Fundamental Rights.
2. Such a law is void ab initio.
3. The law revives if the inconsistency with the Fundamental Right is later removed.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Under Article 13(1), inconsistent pre-Constitution laws are not dead; they are overshadowed and become dormant to the extent of the inconsistency (Bhikaji Narain Dhakras, 1955). They revive when the shadow is removed.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 14:
1. 'Equal protection of the laws' is a concept borrowed from British law.
2. Article 14 is available to non-citizens as well.
3. Reasonable classification is permitted if it rests on an intelligible differentia having a rational nexus with the object of the law.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: 'Equality before law' is the British concept, and 'equal protection of the laws' comes from the US Constitution. Article 14 says 'any person', so foreigners are covered.

questions.q:
With reference to the Indra Sawhney judgment (1992), consider the following:
1. It upheld the 27 per cent reservation for OBCs in central government posts.
2. It held that reservations should not generally exceed 50 per cent.
3. It required exclusion of the creamy layer among OBCs.
4. It extended reservation in promotions to OBCs.

Which of the above are correct?
questions.e: The Court held that Article 16(4) reservation applies to initial appointments, not promotions. Parliament later enabled reservation in promotions for SCs and STs through the 77th Amendment (Article 16(4A)).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 103rd Constitution Amendment Act, 2019:
1. It inserted clause (6) in both Article 15 and Article 16.
2. Its validity was upheld by the Supreme Court in Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India (2022).
3. Its benefits extend to economically weaker persons belonging to the SC, ST and OBC categories.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The 10 per cent EWS reservation is meant for sections not covered by existing reservations under Articles 15(4), 15(5) and 16(4). The Constitution Bench upheld the amendment by a 3:2 majority.

questions.q:
With reference to Article 18 of the Constitution, consider the following statements:
1. The State cannot confer any title except a military or academic distinction.
2. A citizen of India cannot accept any title from a foreign State.
3. A non-citizen holding an office of profit under the State may accept a foreign title without any consent.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: A non-citizen holding an office of profit under the State needs the President's consent to accept a foreign title. Bharat Ratna and Padma awards are not 'titles' (Balaji Raghavan, 1996).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 19:
1. The six freedoms are available to citizens only.
2. The freedom to acquire, hold and dispose of property was deleted from Article 19 by the 44th Amendment.
3. The 97th Amendment added the right to form cooperative societies to Article 19(1)(c).
4. Freedom of the press is expressly mentioned in Article 19(1)(a).

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Freedom of the press is not expressly mentioned. The Court derived it from the freedom of speech and expression. Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a ground for imposing reasonable restrictions on freedom of speech and expression under Article 19(2)?
questions.e: 'Interests of the general public' is a ground under Article 19(5) and 19(6) (movement, residence, profession), not 19(2). 'Public order' was added by the 1st Amendment, 1951. Section 66A of the IT Act was struck down in Shreya Singhal (2015).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 20:
1. Protection under Article 20 cannot be suspended during a National Emergency.
2. The protection against ex post facto laws applies to civil laws as well.
3. The protection against double jeopardy bars prosecution and punishment for the same offence more than once.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended even in an Emergency (44th Amendment). Ex post facto protection covers only criminal laws; civil and tax laws can be retrospective.

questions.q:
Which of the following have been held by the Supreme Court to be part of the right to life under Article 21?
1. Right to privacy
2. Right to speedy trial
3. Right to livelihood
4. Right to strike
questions.e: Privacy (Puttaswamy, 2017), speedy trial (Hussainara Khatoon) and livelihood (Olga Tellis) were read into Article 21. The right to strike is not a fundamental right (T.K. Rangarajan, 2003).

questions.q:
With reference to Article 22, consider the following statements:
1. The protections for arrested persons in Article 22(1) and (2) are not available to persons detained under preventive detention laws.
2. Parliament may prescribe the maximum period for which a person can be detained under a preventive detention law.
3. Only Parliament, and not the State legislatures, can make laws on preventive detention.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Preventive detention for security of the State, public order and essential supplies is on the Concurrent List, so States can legislate. Only defence and foreign-affairs-related detention is Parliament's exclusive field.

questions.q:
With reference to Articles 23 and 24, consider the following statements:
1. Article 23 protects against exploitation by private individuals as well as by the State.
2. Article 23 permits the State to impose compulsory service for public purposes.
3. Article 24 prohibits employment of children below 18 years in any hazardous occupation.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Supreme Court (PUDR v. Union of India, 1982) held that Article 23 operates against private persons too. Article 24 covers children below 14 years; the Child Labour Amendment Act, 2016 prohibits all work below 14 and hazardous work below 18.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the freedom of religion:
1. The right to propagate religion under Article 25 does not include a right to convert another person.
2. The doctrine of essential religious practices was articulated in the Shirur Mutt case (1954).
3. Article 28(1) prohibits religious instruction in all educational institutions recognised by the State.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Rev. Stainislaus v. State of MP (1977) held there is no fundamental right to convert. Article 28(1) bars religious instruction only in institutions wholly maintained by State funds.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Articles 29 and 30:
1. Article 29(1) protects any section of citizens having a distinct language, script or culture.
2. Article 30(1) gives minorities, based on religion or language, the right to establish and administer educational institutions.
3. Article 30(2) bars the State from discriminating in granting aid on the ground that an institution is under minority management.
4. Minority institutions are exempt from all State regulation of academic standards.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Minority institutions are subject to reasonable regulation to ensure academic standards, as the Court held in T.M.A. Pai Foundation (2002) and later cases.

questions.q:
With reference to the writs issued under Article 32, consider the following statements:
1. Prohibition is issued to stop a lower court from exceeding its jurisdiction while proceedings are pending.
2. Certiorari is issued to quash an order already passed by a lower court or tribunal.
3. Quo warranto can be sought only by a person personally aggrieved by the appointment.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Prohibition acts during proceedings and certiorari after a decision. Anyone, not only an aggrieved person, can move quo warranto, since it tests the legality of a claim to a public office.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The 44th Amendment removed the right to property from the list of Fundamental Rights and made it a legal right under Article 300A.
2. Laws placed in the Ninth Schedule are completely immune from judicial review.
3. The Ninth Schedule was added by the First Constitutional Amendment, 1951.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: In I.R. Coelho (2007), the Supreme Court held that laws placed in the Ninth Schedule after 24 April 1973 can be tested against the basic structure and Fundamental Rights.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the relationship between Fundamental Rights and the Directive Principles:
1. In Champakam Dorairajan (1951), the Court held that Directive Principles must run as subsidiary to Fundamental Rights.
2. In Minerva Mills (1980), the Court held that harmony and balance between the two is part of the basic structure.
3. In Minerva Mills, the Court upheld the extension of Article 31C to all Directive Principles by the 42nd Amendment.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The 42nd Amendment's extension of Article 31C to all Directive Principles was struck down in Minerva Mills. Only laws giving effect to Article 39(b) and (c) retain that protection.

questions.q:
Which of the following Directive Principles are based on Gandhian ideas?
1. Organising village panchayats
2. Securing a uniform civil code
3. Prohibition of intoxicating drinks
4. Promotion of cottage industries
questions.e: Articles 40, 43 and 47 (among others) are Gandhian. The uniform civil code (Article 44) is classed as a liberal-intellectual principle.

questions.q:
Match the Articles with their subjects:

A. Article 40
B. Article 41
C. Article 46
D. Article 47

1. Right to work and public assistance in specified cases
2. Organisation of village panchayats
3. Raising the level of nutrition, standard of living and public health
4. Promotion of educational and economic interests of SCs, STs and weaker sections
questions.e: Article 40: village panchayats. Article 41: right to work, education and public assistance. Article 46: SC/ST and weaker sections. Article 47: nutrition, living standards and public health.

questions.q:
With reference to the Uniform Civil Code, consider the following statements:
1. Article 44 directs the State to endeavour to secure a uniform civil code for citizens throughout India.
2. Goa has had a common family law inherited from the Portuguese Civil Code.
3. Article 44 makes the uniform civil code enforceable by the courts.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Article 44 is in Part IV, which Article 37 declares non-justiciable. Uttarakhand enacted a UCC law in 2024, brought into force in January 2025.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a Directive Principle of State Policy?
o: Equal pay for equal work for both men and women
Equal justice and free legal aid
Protection of monuments of national importance
questions.e: These are Article 39(d), Article 39A and Article 49. There is no constitutional right to strike, and it is not a Directive Principle either.

questions.q: Article 51 directs the State to endeavour to do all of the following EXCEPT:
o: promote military alliances with friendly nations
maintain just and honourable relations between nations
encourage settlement of international disputes by arbitration
questions.e: Article 51 covers peace and security, just and honourable relations, respect for international law and treaty obligations, and settlement of disputes by arbitration. Military alliances are not mentioned.

questions.q:
Which of the following Directive Principles were added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976?
1. Equal justice and free legal aid
2. Participation of workers in the management of industries
3. Protection and improvement of the environment
4. Promotion of cooperative societies
questions.e: The 42nd Amendment added Articles 39A, 43A and 48A. Article 43B (cooperative societies) was added by the 97th Amendment, 2011.

questions.q:
With reference to Article 40 and Panchayati Raj, consider the following statements:
1. Article 40 directs the State to organise village panchayats.
2. The 73rd Amendment added Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule listing 29 subjects.
3. Elections to panchayats are conducted by the Election Commission of India.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Panchayat elections are conducted by the State Election Commission (Article 243K), not by the Election Commission of India.

questions.q:
Which of the following contain directives to the State outside Part IV of the Constitution?
1. Instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage for linguistic minorities (Article 350A)
2. Promotion of the spread of the Hindi language (Article 351)
3. Claims of SCs and STs to services and posts (Article 335)
questions.e: Besides Part IV, these three articles carry directives to the State.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Fundamental Duties:
1. They were added by the 42nd Amendment on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.
2. There were originally ten duties, and a later amendment added an eleventh.
3. They are justiciable and enforceable by the courts.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The duties are in Part IVA (Article 51A) and are non-justiciable. The 86th Amendment (2002) added the eleventh duty, 51A(k).

questions.q: Which one of the following is a Fundamental Duty under Article 51A?
o: To exercise the franchise in every election
To safeguard public property and abjure violence
questions.e: Article 51A(i) requires citizens to safeguard public property and abjure violence. Paying taxes and voting are legal obligations or choices, not listed duties.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002:
1. It inserted Article 21A, providing free and compulsory education for children aged 6-14.
2. It changed Article 45 to require early childhood care and education for children below six.
3. It added a Fundamental Duty on parents or guardians to provide educational opportunities to children aged 6-14.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: All three are correct. The duty is Article 51A(k). The Right to Education Act, 2009 gives effect to Article 21A.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Fundamental Duties:
1. Courts may take them into account when judging the reasonableness of a restriction on a Fundamental Right.
2. Parliament may give effect to them through legislation, such as the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971.
3. They apply to all persons in India, including foreigners.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Article 51A is addressed to 'every citizen'. Courts have used the duties as interpretive aids (for example AIIMS Students' Union, 2001), and statutes can enforce them.

questions.q:
Which of the following are Fundamental Duties of citizens?
1. To develop scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform
2. To strive towards excellence in individual and collective activity
3. To protect and improve the natural environment
4. To promote industrial growth
questions.e: These are Article 51A(h), (j) and (g). Promoting industrial growth is not a listed duty.
